analysis:
Documentation-only change in docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md: the date bump (head line 3) and a new paragraph (head lines 784-790). The paragraph says a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates its destinations already available from host bytes. It evaluates and fences none of them, so staging does not wait on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. The import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift).

This is an exception to the base text at lines 776-783. There, checkpoint staging/import holds a noncharging WholeMacUnboundedActivity so deadline forecasts do not mistake that activity for an idle GPU. The new text does not say whether host-staged imports still hold WholeMacUnboundedActivity. If they do not, the effect is accuracy of availability/routing signals, not confidentiality. The read-scratch charge also changes memory-admission accounting, which relates to T-041 mitigation (e) on transient staging reservations.

Authentication-before-staging claims in the base text (lines 719-731) are unchanged. These cover manifest authentication, whole-file authentication while filling the destination, and "only a fully authenticated matched checkpoint is staged". cacheSalt scoping, HMAC naming and TTL are also unchanged, so T-041 posture appears unaffected.

No source code was supplied. The integration pass should verify in CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift and SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Read.swift that:
- host-byte destinations are populated only after AES-GCM authentication of the whole file, not exposed to the engine before the tag check;
- the scratch charge bounds the actual allocation.

The second point bears on memory DoS (T-041 (e)). No concrete regression is visible in the docs alone.
